text_blocks.snippet: Jardiance (empagliflozin) can cause common, manageable side effects as well as rare, serious complications linked to how it removes excess sugar through the urine.

list.snippet: Increased urination and thirst: Passing more urine and feeling thirstier happen because the medication forces your kidneys to flush out extra blood sugar.

Genital yeast (fungal) infections: Extra sugar in the urine can cause yeast infections in women (vaginal itching, burning, thick white discharge) and men (redness, itching, or swelling around the penis or scrotum).
Urinary tract infections (UTIs): Symptoms include a burning sensation when urinating, a strong or frequent urge to go, and cloudy or discolored urine.

Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA): A dangerous buildup of acid in the blood that can occur even if blood sugar levels are not severely high. Watch for nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual fatigue, fruity-smelling breath, or trouble breathing.
Severe dehydration and low blood pressure: Fluid loss can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting—especially if you are older, take water pills (diuretics), or have kidney issues.

Necrotizing fasciitis (Fournier's gangrene): A rare, life-threatening bacterial infection of the tissue under the skin in the perineum (between the genitals and anus) causing severe pain, redness, swelling, and fever.
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia): More likely if Jardiance is taken alongside other diabetes medications like insulin or sulfonylureas.
Serious allergic reactions: Symptoms include hives, rash, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, and throat.

text_blocks.snippet: For detailed safety guidelines and medication guides, consult the Jardiance Official Safety Information or review an overview on GoodRx Side Effects Guide.
